action: cross-verify our proofs with an independent implementation
metric: snarkjs: honest ACCEPT (OK), 4 mutations refused (public input +1, pi_a.y +1, vk IC +1, public[0]=0)
note: Tier 4 was the documented gap: 'this proof verifies' rested on one implementation. Groth16 over BN254 is a standard, the arkworks encoding is not, so the work was a conversion: hex->decimal, G1 [x,y,'1'], G2 [[c0,c1],[c0,c1],['1','0']], nPublic=IC-1, circuit order preserved, vk_alphabeta_12 unused by the verifier. Answer to 'how big is Tier 4': a day, not a month.

action: cost the trace_digest Merkle binding before implementing it
metric: 660 constraints per 2-to-1 MiMC node; depth 3 = 1,980 (circuit 3,333 -> 5,313, 1.59x); prove 0.061s -> ~0.09s
note: MAX_ACTIONS=8, so a v0 transcript has 8 leaves and needs depth 3 -- the depth 8/12 options were costed against a tree the protocol cannot produce. Costing it first turned a scary circuit change into a measured 1.59x. A depth-cost probe is cheaper than a design argument.
